title: Orchestrate company OKRs via initiative signal-bus and scarcity-aware prioritization
creator: Amira Patel
description:
Problem statement: Cross-functional teams repeatedly surface competing initiatives that map to company OKRs but are hard to compare because requests arrive in different formats, use different success metrics, and surface resource needs only at the last minute. This causes late reprioritization, scope churn, and missed OKR targets.

Goal: Create an operational pattern and lightweight system called the 'initiative signal-bus' plus a scarcity-aware prioritization process that converts company OKRs into comparable initiative requests, surfaces resource contention early, and provides deterministic escalation and gating rules for roadmap planning across quarterly waves.

Scope: The work covers a) a canonical initiative manifest and schema for teams to publish signals, b) a central registry (document + lightweight dashboard) that consumes signals and computes a scarcity-aware score, c) a decision rubric + runbook for roadmap planners and execs, and d) templates and training for PMs and Eng leads. Not in scope: building a full engineering-backed service or automating funding approvals in this phase.

Success metrics:
- Reduce cross-team roadmap reprioritization events that require exec intervention by 60% within two quarters.
- 90% of initiatives that map to company-level OKRs publish a valid signal using the manifest during the intake window for a quarterly wave.
- Average time to resolve resource contention tickets lowered from 7 days to 48 hours for prioritized initiatives.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical initiative manifest (JSON + human-readable guide) exists and is approved by PM, Eng, Design leadership.
An initial 'initiative registry' document and lightweight dashboard (Confluence + Looker/console prototype) shows accepted signals and computed scarcity scores.
Decision rubric and gating runbook published with clear thresholds for canary/cutback/escalation and sign-off roles.
Training session materials and templates delivered; at least three pilot teams use the flow in the next quarterly planning window.
Post-pilot retrospective with measurable changes to reprioritization events and conflict resolution time recorded.
tasks: Draft initiative manifest (fields: objective mapping, primary metric, expected outcome, required headcount, infra/GPU impact, start/finish, dependencies). Owner: Amira. Due: 2025-11-22.
Prototype registry doc and dashboard wiring (Confluence + embeddings into console). Owner: Rafael. Due: 2025-11-30.
Define scarcity-aware scoring formula (capacity shadowing + OKR weight + risk multiplier). Owner: Eng Analytics. Due: 2025-12-08.
Hold cross-functional review and sign-off (PM, Eng, Design, Finance). Owner: Amira. Due: 2025-12-12.
Pilot with three initiatives from infra, runtime, and console teams. Owner: Rafael. Cycle: Q1 planning window.
Produce runbook and escalation flow with decision owners and SLAs. Owner: PM Ops. Due: 2025-12-20.
Deliver training session and capture feedback. Owner: DE/Training. Due: 2025-12-28.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Teams may treat the manifest as additional paperwork and skip signals. Mitigation: keep manifest minimal, provide templates and PM-to-PM onboarding; require signal for initiative intake cutoff.
Risk: Scarcity scoring is perceived as black-box. Mitigation: publish scoring formula with worked examples and allow manual override with documented justification and exec approval path.
Risk: Dashboard adoption lags. Mitigation: embed a daily digest in PM slack channel and automate conflict alerts during intake windows.
Risk: Dependencies on ENG and DES bandwidth for pilot. Mitigation: limit pilot to three initiatives and negotiate time-boxed support commitments with Eng leadership.
notes: Design trade-off: preferred lightweight approach is a human-first registry + computed score rather than a mandatory API for initial rollout.
We will evaluate automating signals ingestion into the Console in phase 2 if adoption > 60% in pilot.
Related initiative: resource-forecasting proof-of-concept under ENG-5012 should feed capacity estimates into the scoring formula.
